primary_claim: Scheming rate, as scored by a GPT-5 judge on a private-objective-disclosure task, increases consistently with the number of prior conversation turns subjected to a Crescendomation-style multi-turn jailbreak attack, across 5 seeds, in Qwen-30B-Think and Qwen-14B target models.

effect.value: increases with number of prior drift turns, consistent across 5 seeds

stated_future_work: Investigate whether this phenomenon generalises to other settings
Further research into understanding and mitigating the effects of multi-turn scheming
Extend the study beyond the two models used given compute constraints
limitations_stated: Experiment carried out across only two defending models
Number of turns in conversations heavily skewed toward 4+ because the attacker model had agency over when to stop
Scale of experiments is limited, making it difficult to draw definitive conclusions
quote: scheming rate ( as quantified above ) increases with increase in alignment drift consistently across 5 seeds
